I checked all six problems against the code on jusprin-dev and against the real Ollama 0.40.18 on this Mac. All six are real. I haven't changed any code yet. Three of the fixes show a new sentence, so they need your yes. The other three use only words that are already approved, or the other side's own words.

**1. A local model's own error is reported as ours.** Someone chats with a model in Ollama, and Ollama refuses the request. Maybe the model was deleted (Ollama answers 404: "model 'no-such-model:1b' not found", which I saw on this Mac), or it's too big for memory (500: "llama runner process has terminated"). Today the person sees "Something went wrong on our side", and we get a report. The failure is theirs. **Fix:** show Ollama's own words in the existing format, for example: Ollama says: "model 'x' not found". No report. This also covers the same refusal during the model check in Preferences, and LM Studio's errors when they come in the same form.

**2. A wrong address or an older Ollama is reported as ours.** Someone enters port 5000. On a Mac, something else answers there with 403 and an empty body. Today that's "Something went wrong on our side". **Fix:** any answer that isn't Ollama or LM Studio talking shows the approved sentence: "Nothing is answering at <address>. Start Ollama or LM Studio, then try again." One limit: someone running an Ollama too old to have the chat endpoint gets this sentence too, and it doesn't tell them to update. I'd accept that rather than add a fourth sentence.

**3. A failed save while switching profile opens our report dialog.** Someone has the cut tool open and picks another printer or filament. The app must save a version before dropping their setting changes. The save refuses because a tool is open, and they're told "Something went wrong on our side", though closing the tool fixes it. **Fix:** stop the switch and show a new sentence. When the AI made the switch, the AI is told instead and asks the person to close the tool. Save failures that really are ours are reported once, by the code that started the work: no dialog during an AI tool call, and one window instead of two when opening a project.

**4. A timed-out setup command is recognised only in English.** Someone connects an outside AI app such as Claude Code, and its command runs past 30 seconds. In English they're told that settings might have changed and shown the file. In German or any other language the app looks for the English words "timed out" and doesn't find them. So it shows "Copy the command and run it yourself" and drops the warning. **Fix:** the command passes back a timed-out flag, and the app checks the flag. No wording changes.

**5. A chat too long for the model gives no next step.** Today it says "The request was too large for the <service> service." **Fix:** a new sentence that says to start a new chat.

**6. An outage at the person's own AI service reads like a network problem.** OpenAI, OpenRouter or Anthropic answers 500 or more, or reports an overload mid-reply. The person sees "The AI request could not reach the <service> service", the same sentence they'd see with no network, so they go and check their own connection. **Fix:** a new sentence that puts the trouble at the service. Retry stays available. A key check that hits an outage still says nothing about whether the key is good.

**Decision needed:** do you approve these three new sentences? Each will have translations in JusPrin's own catalogs and a test.
- For the save refused because a tool is open (problem 3): "An editing tool is open. Close it, then try again."
- For the chat too long (problem 5): "This chat is too long for the <service> service. Start a new chat to continue." This also covers a chat with too many pictures, where a new chat is also the way out.
- For the outage (problem 6): "The <service> service is having trouble right now. Try again later." This is the audit's wording, and I'd keep it.

You can approve them, or give your own wording for any of them. Once you confirm, I'll reproduce each problem, fix it in a new worktree from `origin/jusprin-dev`, and commit one fix or one small group of related fixes per commit, quoting your words wherever a sentence needed your yes. # JusPrin's translations

JusPrin shows its interface in the languages OrcaSlicer ships a catalog for
(`languages.json`). OrcaSlicer's own windows translate through upstream's
catalogs in `localization/i18n/`, which the fork never edits. JusPrin's own
text has catalogs of its own here, so taking a new OrcaSlicer release never
conflicts in a translation file:

| Text | Marked with | Catalog | How it reaches the app |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Native windows and text the native side sends to a page | `_L`, `_u8L`, `L`, `_L_CONTEXT`, `_L_PLURAL`, `translated_plural` | `native/<lang>.po`, template `native/JusPrin.pot` | `Brand/brand_catalogs.py` merges it into `resources/i18n/<lang>/<app key>.mo`, the catalog the app loads |
| The AI and Home pages | Lingui macros: `t`, `plural` from `@lingui/core/macro`; `Trans`, `Plural` from `@lingui/react/macro` | `pages/<lang>.po`, one for both pages | `@lingui/vite-plugin` compiles every catalog into each page; the page reads `?lang=` (`AgentUI/src/i18n.tsx`) |

Native text that OrcaSlicer's template already has is left out of
`native/JusPrin.pot`; upstream's translation is used.

Text the fork takes from upstream before upstream's catalogs have it, such as
a cherry-picked fix with a new message, would reach the person in English.
`update_catalogs.py` also reads the OrcaSlicer files listed in its
`UPSTREAM_AHEAD`; their text missing from OrcaSlicer's template becomes JusPrin
entries, and leaves again once upstream's template has it. Add a file there
when taking such a change, and remove it once upstream's catalogs carry its
text.

